pr_title: sql: avoid hydration when looking up non-type descriptor within hydration cache
pr_body:
Fixes #93314

When creating a UDF whose signature uses implicit record type which has a column of user defined enum type, crdb crashes because of a type hydration deadloop. The reason is that when we try to hydrate the implicit record type, the enum type also needs to be hydrated, and the schema descriptor as well because we need a fully qualified type name which requires a schema lookup and we now have function signatures within schema descriptor which has the type information. Then to hydrate the schema descriptor, the function signature types need to hydrated (again!), such the deadloop happens.

This pr adds a new flag for descriptor lookup to explicitly avoid hydration when looking up descriptor that can't be used as a UDT, so that we can avoid the hydration deadloop when looking up schema descriptor for its name.

Release note (sql change): Previously, cockroach db would crash if user creates a UDF whose function signature includes a implicit record type (essentially a table) which has a column using a user defined enum type. This root cause was that there was  a hydration deadloop when looking up descriptors during hydration. This PR adds a new flag to avoid hydration in order to avoid the deadloop, users shouldn't feel differentce on using UDFs.

issue_context.title: Creating a function that returns a table type containing an enum type crashes the server
issue_context.body:
**Describe the problem**

Create a function that returns a table type, which contains an enum type. The creation of the function crashes the server

**To Reproduce**

```sql
create type e as enum ('a', 'b');
create table t (i int, e e);
insert into t values (1, 'a');

create or replace function f () returns t as 
$$
select i, e
from t
order by i
limit 1;
$$
language sql;
```

After this, the server is gone completely. It appears I also can't start it again!

**Expected behavior**

No crash

**Environment:**
 - CockroachDB version: CockroachDB CCL v22.2.0 (x86_64-pc-linux-gnu, built 2022/12/05 16:37:36, go1.19.1)
 - Server OS: Linux (Docker)
 - Client app: Dbeaver (JDBC)


Jira issue: CRDB-22270

review_comments:
I find that this added boolean argument makes `MakeTypeLookupFuncForHydration` really hard to reason about, especially now that it returns a recursive function. Instead can we make it so that the `HydrationLookupFunc` implementations _always_ set `SkipHydration` so that we _know_ that all `lookupFn` calls don't recurse further into the hydration logic?

This requires pulling some logic from the `hydrateDescriptors` method in `descs.Collection` into the recursive function returned by `MakeTypeLookupFuncForHydration` (specifically, after `typDesc, err = lookupFn(ctx, id, false /* skipHydration */)`), but that's probably a good thing anyway and will probably simplify code that's already complicated instead of complicating it further.
I'll look into this in a bit.

Sorry just came back to this...was looking at other issues. I think the right way to `hydrate a slice of descriptors` is that
(1). go through all target descriptors to figure out what types are need. this would just require getting all interested type OID/IDs. There this no look up needed. Simply just get all IDs. I don't think there'll be recursions. It's simply loop through each descriptor type internally to get types. Though there could be 2 or 3 levels. For example, for function, we'd need to go through args and return type, and if any of these type is a table, we need to go through all the visible table columns.

(2). then we construct a data structure which would contain all the types required with the IDs we get in (1). Here, we need to make sure all types are hydrated. Actually, `hydrating a type` seems the wrong concept here. Only table implicit record type needs hydration. So that, we could lookup all type descriptors first and memoize them in the new data structure. And then, we hydrate the table or implicit record type with the the type descriptors we already have. Now, we have all the types. 
-- There shouldn't be any recursion. Because:
    1> type descriptors doesn't need hydration, or 1 level hydration at most.
    2> table implicit record type only need 1 level hydration, because we can't use record type with in record type yet, and composite type can't use enum yet. Well, the worst case is that things can be very explicit.

(3) simply replace all the type references in each descriptor with the types we all ready got. there is not recursion.

Let me know what you think... But anyhow I don't think I can commit to this now. We can do this later.
I think that you're completely correct. I'll be happy to do what you suggested as a follow-up to this PR.
Should we also upsert `c` with all the other descriptors we look up, now that this function is recursive?
good idea, I think we can do that.
`Hydrate` is not thread-safe, should we be concerned?

Ignoring my concerns about the `skipHydration` boolean argument you probably should retrieve a hydrated descriptor using `lookupFn(ctx, id, false /* skipHydration */)` rather than calling `Hydrate` directly.

I'm afraid that we need to do `Hydrate` because [this path](https://github.com/cockroachdb/cockroach/blob/cf1e7e6bc6ef9e55510b9ed13bd068bb3894cd92/pkg/sql/catalog/descs/hydrate.go#L169-L169) (used by show backup) really doesn't lookup anything, I'm assuming they have all descriptors in the fast lookup catalog....

> Hydrate is not thread-safe, should we be concerned?

Hmm...I'll need to think about this.
Where does multi-threading come into the picture here?
I think we're fine here, The only thing shared across threads regarding this hydration domain is the hydrated descriptor cache and that is thread safe.
